questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The launch of the small electric car will depend to the willingness of buyers to pay more for it.

options.text: of buyers to pay more for it

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3.**
 
• The error lies in the wrong usage of the preposition 'to' which is used to determine the movement. 'to' should be replaced by **'on' which indicates the state of something. The verb 'depend' takes the preposition 'on'.**
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence is 'The launch of the small electric car will depend **on** the willingness of buyers to pay more for it.'

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The merchant took out the dead parrot from the cage.

options.text: The dead parrot is taken out from the cage by the merchant.
The dead parrot was taking out from the cage by the merchant.
The dead parrot was taken out from the cage by the merchant.
The dead parrot took out from the cage by the merchant.

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 3.**
 
• The structure of the given active sentence is 'Subject+V2+object+other words'.
 
• The structure of the passive sentence should be '**Object+was/were+V3+other words'.**
 
• Option 1 is wrong because the verb 'is' is used instead of 'was'.
 
• Option 2 is wrong because of the wrong usage of the verb 'taking out'.a
 
• Option 4 is wrong because the verb is in 2nd form i.e. 'took'.
 
• **The only option which satisfies the structure is 'Option 3' i.e. 'The dead parrot was taken out from the cage by the merchant.'**

questions.question:

questions.solution:
• **The correct answer is Option 2 i.e. 'clear'.**
 
• The meaning of the given words:
 
• Opaque: Unclear, Difficult to see through.
 
• Hazy: Thick or obscure; not clear or transparent.
 
• Clear: Transparent, bright, obvious.
 
• Frosty: Cold, chilly.
 
• Dull: Boring, not exciting or interesting, not shiny.
 
• **Therefore, it is obvious that the antonym of the given word 'opaque' is 'clear'.**

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Bhola said to his mother, "Why is this charcoal so black?"

options.text: Bhola told his mother why that charcoal was so black.
Bhola asked his mother why the charcoal is so black.
Bhola asked his mother why that charcoal was so black.
Bhola asked his mother why was that charcoal so black.

questions.solution: The correct answer is **Option 3. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** The given sentence is an interrogative statement in **Direct speech**. It needs to be converted into the indirect speech. When we convert a sentence from the direct to the indirect mode, the following changes take place: • The Reported verb 'Said to' is changed to 'asked' as it is an interrogative form. • The tense of the reporting speech 'is' is changed to 'was'. • The given sentence is in** interrogative form** while changing to indirect sentence it becomes** an assertive sentence.** • Thus the indirect speech sentence is: *Bhola asked his mother why that charcoal was so black.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. But after a while they all began to blur in our memories.

B. When we arrived in Bangkok, we took a tour of the city's famous Buddhist temples.

C. However there was one temple, the Temple of Golden Buddha, which left an indelible impression in our hearts and minds.

D. We visited numerous temples that day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** BDAC.**

 
• Among the given jumbled sentences, the only independent sentence we have is sentence B.
 
• Sentence D is talking about visiting temples which is continued in sentence A. Lastly, the overall opinion is given in sentence C
 
• **Therefore, the sequence is correctly followed in option 4 i.e. BDAC**

questions.question:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order.

A. There was an old apple tree in the centre of a village.

B. The adults also sat in the shade and discussed important things.

C. They remembered that they too had played around the tree when they were young.

D. Children loved to play around the tree and pick delicious apples.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 1 i.e. ADBC.**

FIrst try to find out the starting sentence. 

C will not be the first one because it starts with a **pronoun.**

D and C will not be the first one because both are talking about the tree and shade respectively.

A will be the first sentence as it introduces the main noun of the passage.

Now we have two option starting with A.

after A, C will not come because It is not clear what THEY is used for.

So, the option 3 is out and answer will be option 1.
